rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ‘forgetting’ means treating them as forgotten; nothing escapes His knowledge and He does not literally forget.
rows.anchor: ولا ينساه، كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is reciprocal requital, as in passages saying God forgets those who forget Him or the Last Day.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال تعالى هذا من باب المقابلة، كما قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God forgets them with respect to good, but does not forget them with respect to evil.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس في [قوله] (8) {فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا} قال: نسيهم الله من الخير، ولم ينسهم من الشر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God leaves them as they left the meeting with this Day.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قال: نتركهم، كما تركوا لقاء يومهم هذا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God leaves them in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نتركهم في النار.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: God leaves them without mercy because they left acting in preparation for meeting this Day.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: نتركهم من الرحمة، كما تركوا أن يعملوا للقاء يومهم هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ describes God reminding a servant of His gifts; after the servant denies expecting to meet Him, God says He will forget him as he forgot God.
rows.anchor: في الصحيح أن الله تعالى يقول للعبد يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's creation and rule and directing people to pray to Him, the passage points to Him as provider and raiser of the dead.
rows.anchor: نبه تعالى على أنه الرزاق، وأنه يعيد الموتى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds spread before the rain-bearing clouds.
rows.anchor: أي: ناشرة بين يدي السحاب الحامل للمطر

rows.speaker: قراء غير مسمين
rows.claim: Some read the word as بشرا, understood alongside the description of winds as bearers of good tidings.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قرأ {بشرا} كقوله {ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Before His mercy’ means before the rain, supported by verses describing rainfall and the revival of dead earth as God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {بين يدي رحمته} أي: بين يدي المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds lift clouds heavy with abundant water; they become weighty, low to the earth, and dark.
rows.anchor: أي: من كثرة ما فيها من الماء، تكون ثقيلة قريبة من الأرض مدلهمة، كما قال زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، رحمه الله.

rows.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
rows.claim: A poem depicts clouds carrying sweet, pure water and the earth carrying heavy rocks, illustrating the imagery of weighty clouds.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، رحمه الله. وأسلمت وجهي لمن أسلمت … له المزن تحمل عذبا زلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dead land is barren and has no vegetation, as another verse describes the dead earth being revived.
rows.anchor: أرض ميتة، مجدبة (4) لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving barren earth illustrates bodily resurrection: rain will fall for forty days and bodies will grow in their graves like seed in soil; this is a recurring Qur'anic analogy.
rows.anchor: ينزل الله، سبحانه وتعالى، ماء من السماء، فتمطر الأرض أربعين يوما، فتنبت منه الأجساد في قبورها كما ينبت الحب في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good earth produces its vegetation quickly and well, as the verse about Mary says God caused her to grow well.
rows.anchor: أي: والأرض الطيبة يخرج نباتها سريعا حسنا

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: The land that yields only poor growth is exemplified by salt marshes and similar ground.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره: كالسباخ ونحوها.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The contrast between good and foul land is a parable for the believer and disbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في الآية: هذا مثل ضربه الله للمؤمن والكافر.

rows.speaker: أبو موسى عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet compares his guidance and knowledge to rain: receptive fertile soil produces abundant growth, soil that stores water benefits others, and barren flats retain or grow nothing; likewise people differ in understanding, teaching, and accepting God's guidance. Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Nasa'i transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "مثل ما بعثني الله به من الهدى والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's chiefs accuse Moses and his people of corrupting Pharaoh's subjects by calling them to worship God; the irony is that Pharaoh's party are the real corrupters, though unaware.
rows.anchor: ألا إن فرعون وقومه هم المفسدون، ولكن لا يشعرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the waw as circumstantial: ‘while they have left your worship and your gods?’
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: "الواو" هنا حالية

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy recited a variant making explicit that they had left Pharaoh to worship him and his gods; Ibn Jarir records it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ذلك أبي بن كعب: "وقد تركوك أن يعبدوك وآلهتك"، حكاه ابن جرير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpreters take the waw as conjunction: the chiefs urge Pharaoh not to let Moses and his people continue their corruption and their abandonment of Pharaoh's gods.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي عاطفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: A reading of إلاهتك means ‘your worship’; it is also reported from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "إلاهتك" أي: عبادتك، وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس ومجاهد.

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: On the reading ‘your gods,’ Hasan says Pharaoh secretly worshipped a deity; another account says he wore a jewel on his neck and bowed to it.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن البصري: كان لفرعون إله يعبده في السر

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: In another report, Pharaoh had a pendant jewel on his neck and prostrated to it.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية أخرى: كان له (2) جمانة في عنقه معلقة يسجد لها.

rows.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The gods attributed to Pharaoh were cattle: he made his people worship any beautiful cow they saw, which explains his producing a calf for them.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي في قوله تعالى: {ويذرك وآلهتك} وآلهته، فيما زعم ابن عباس، كانت البقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh renews the order to kill Israelite sons and spare daughters, repeating an earlier policy from before Moses' birth; the intended oppression instead ends in Israel's victory and Pharaoh's humiliation and drowning.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر ثان بهذا الصنيع، وقد كان نكل بهم به قبل ولادة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses tells his people to seek God's help and remain patient, promising that God grants the earth to whom He wills and that the righteous will prevail.
rows.anchor: ووعدهم بالعاقبة، وأن الدار ستصير لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people say they suffered before and after Moses came; he points them from their present distress to the hoped-for destruction of the enemy and succession in the land, urging gratitude when relief comes.
rows.anchor: وهذا تحضيض لهم على العزم على الشكر، عند حلول النعم وزوال النقم

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda explains أسف as the most intense anger.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء "الأسف": أشد الغضب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses rebukes them for the evil way they succeeded him by worshipping the calf after he left.
rows.anchor: يقول: بئس ما صنعتم في عبادتكم العجل بعد أن ذهبت وتركتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks why they hastened his return; its timing had been decreed by God.
rows.anchor: يقول: استعجلتم مجيئي إليكم، وهو مقدر من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view says the tablets were made of emerald.
rows.anchor: قيل: كانت الألواح من زمرد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view says the tablets were made of ruby.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من ياقوت.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported view says the tablets were made of ice.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The material reports illustrate the principle that direct observation is unlike merely hearing a report.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على ما جاء في الحديث: "ليس الخبر كالمعاينة"

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء سلفا وخلفا
rows.claim: The apparent sequence is that Moses threw the tablets in anger at his people; Ibn Kathir endorses this as the majority view of early and later scholars.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول جمهور العلماء سلفا وخلفا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the strange report attributed by al-Tabari to Qatada as an unsound attribution, likely taken from unreliable People of the Book; Ibn Atiyya and others also reject it.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جرير عن قتادة في هذا قولا غريبا، لا يصح إسناده إلى حكاية قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses grabs Aaron because he fears Aaron failed to restrain the people; the parallel account in Ṭā Hā explains Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel or disobeying.
rows.anchor: خوفا أن يكون قد قصر في نهيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron's address ‘son of my mother’ is meant to make Moses more tender and responsive, though Aaron was his full brother.
rows.anchor: وإلا فهو شقيقه لأبيه وأمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to delight their enemies or count him among the wrongdoers, meaning not to treat him as one of them.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تسقني مساقهم، ولا تخلطني معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses confirms Aaron's innocence after recalling that Aaron had already warned Israel against the calf, then asks God to forgive both brothers and admit them to His mercy.
rows.anchor: فلما تحقق موسى، عليه السلام، براءة ساحة هارون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says Moses did not throw the tablets when God informed him that his people had fallen into trial; seeing them himself moved him to throw them, for seeing is unlike hearing.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي (4) صلى الله عليه وسلم "يرحم (5) الله موسى، ليس المعاين كالمخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's punishment for worshipping the calf was that God did not accept their repentance until some killed others, as related in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: فهو أن الله تعالى لم يقبل لهم توبة، حتى قتل بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan says the humiliation of innovation remains on its adherents' shoulders even if they ride fine mules and horses.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحسن البصري: إن ذل البدعة على أكتافهم، وإن هملجت بهم البغلات، وطقطقت بهم البراذين.

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة الجرمي
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba says the verse applies to every fabricator until the Resurrection; Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reports his recitation and explanation.
rows.anchor: وهكذا روى أيوب السختياني، عن أبي قلابة الجرمي، أنه قرأ هذه الآية: {وكذلك نجزي المفترين}

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says every innovator is humiliated.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: كل صاحب بدعة ذليل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reminds people that God accepts repentance from any sin, including disbelief, polytheism, hypocrisy, and factional opposition.
rows.anchor: يقبل توبة عباده من أي ذنب كان، حتى ولو كان من كفر أو شرك أو نفاق أو شقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the calf episode, the verse addresses Muhammad as the messenger of mercy and prophet of light, promising forgiveness and mercy for those who repent and believe.
rows.anchor: يا محمد، يا رسول الرحمة ونبي النور

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Asked about a man who fornicates with a woman and then marries her, Ibn Masud recited this verse ten times and neither ordered nor forbade the marriage.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود؛ أنه سئل عن ذلك -يعني عن الرجل يزني بالمرأة، ثم يتزوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase says that Moses' anger subsided; he then took the tablets he had thrown in intense anger over the calf worship, out of zeal for God.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى: {ولما سكت} أي: سكن {عن موسى الغضب}

rows.speaker: مفسرون كثيرون
rows.claim: Many commentators say the tablets shattered when Moses threw them and that he later gathered them; some early authorities infer that guidance and mercy remained while the detailed content was lost, and they claim fragments survived in royal treasuries into the Islamic period, a claim Ibn Kathir leaves uncertain.
rows.anchor: يقول كثير من المفسرين: إنها لما ألقاها تكسرت، ثم جمعها بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say Moses found guidance and mercy in the tablets after they were gathered.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال بعض السلف: فوجد فيها هدى ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls it decisive evidence that the tablets, which he says were of heavenly substance, broke when thrown: God says Moses found guidance and mercy in them after taking them back.
rows.anchor: وأما الدليل القاطع على أنها تكسرت حين ألقاها، وهي من جوهر الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘for those who fear their Lord,’ the preposition conveys humility within fear, which is why the verb is construed with ل.
rows.anchor: ضمن الرهبة معنى الخضوع؛ ولهذا عداها باللام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada recounts Moses seeking Ahmad's community: the best and first to Paradise, scripture in their hearts, faith in earlier and later books, struggle against error and the Dajjal, rewarded almsgiving, multiplied good deeds, unrecorded intended sins, answered prayers, and intercession; Moses asks to join them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: في قوله تعالى: {أخذ الألواح} قال: رب، إني أجد في الألواح أمة خير أمة أخرجت للناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God commanded Moses to select seventy men to pray; they asked for a distinction no one before or after would receive, which God disliked, and the earthquake struck.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في تفسير هذه الآية: كان الله أمره أن يختار من قومه سبعين رجلا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the seventy were selected to apologize for calf worship; they demanded to see God openly, so a thunderbolt killed them, and Moses grieved that Israel would blame him for destroying its best men.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إن الله أمر موسى أن يأتيه في ناس من بني إسرائيل، يعتذرون إليه من عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts Moses selecting Israel's best seventy for repentance and purification at Sinai; they heard God's commands from within the cloud, then demanded to see Him and died by a thunderbolt, prompting Moses' plea for Israel.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: اختار موسى من بني إسرائيل سبعين رجلا الخير فالخير

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري عن علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali says Moses, Aaron, Shabr, and Shabbir went to a mountain; after Aaron died, Israelites accused Moses of killing him, chose seventy witnesses, and were struck by the quake after Aaron confirmed God had taken him; God then revived them as prophets. Ibn Kathir calls it very strange, does not know Ammara, and notes another weakly identified route.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: حدثني أبو إسحاق، عن عمارة بن عبد السلولي، عن علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وابن جريج
rows.claim: These authorities say the seventy were struck because they had not separated themselves from the calf-worshippers or forbidden their worship; this fits Moses' question about punishment for the fools' deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وابن جريج: إنما أخذتهم الرجفة لأنهم لم يزايلوا قومهم في عبادتهم العجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وأبو العالية وربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: These authorities interpret فتنة as God's trial, testing, and examination; Ibn Kathir says it has no other meaning here.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وأبو العالية، وربيع بن أنس، وغير واحد من علماء السلف والخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' prayer affirms that command and judgment belong to God alone: He guides or misguides, gives or withholds, and owns all creation and rule.
rows.anchor: يقول: إن الأمر إلا أمرك، وإن الحكم إلا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness means covering sin and not exacting punishment; when paired with mercy, mercy means preventing the forgiven person from repeating sin.
rows.anchor: الغفر هو: الستر، وترك المؤاخذة بالذنب، والرحمة إذا قرنت مع الغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best forgiver because none forgives sins except Him.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first part of Moses' supplication seeks removal of harm; the next asks for the desired good.
rows.anchor: هناك الفصل الأول من الدعاء دفع المحذور، وهذا لتحصيل المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Write for us good in this world and the next’ means decree and establish good for us in both; Ibn Kathir says he explained it earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: أي: أوجب لنا وأثبت لنا فيهما حسنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبو العالية والضحاك وإبراهيم التيمي والسدي وقتادة
rows.claim: These authorities explain هدنا as repenting, returning, and turning back to God; Ibn Kathir says this is also its proper linguistic sense.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، والضحاك، وإبراهيم التيمي، والسدي، وقتادة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report in Ibn Jarir says the Jews were so named because they said ‘we have returned to You’; Ibn Kathir notes that its transmitter Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi is weak.
rows.anchor: عن علي [رضي الله عنه] (3) قال: إنما سميت اليهود لأنهم قالوا: {إنا هدنا إليك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that He sends punishment on whom He wills and that His mercy encompasses everything, then specifies those who receive it as the God-fearing, zakat-givers, and believers in His signs; His actions embody wisdom and justice.
rows.anchor: أي: أفعل ما أشاء، وأحكم ما أريد، ولي الحكمة والعدل في كل ذلك
